get.description:
Lists non-deleted workspace invitations in stable ID order. By default, the
response includes pending, expired, and accepted invitations.
Accepted records are returned only when they can be attributed to an invitation;
historical accepted records without that attribution are not returned. Set status
to return one lifecycle state.

This list reads from an indexed store and is eventually consistent; it does
not guarantee immediate read-your-write. Use the create response or direct
invitation GET when an immediate result is required.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Invitation ID after which to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum invitations to return. The default is 20 and the maximum is 1000.

401.description: Missing or invalid Admin API key.

403.description: Admin API key lacks the required Invitations scope or workspace access.

404.description: The workspace was not found or this feature is unavailable.

429.description: Too many requests. The endpoint quota, an operation protection, or a downstream limit was exceeded. Follow Retry-After when provided.

401.description: Missing or invalid Admin API key.

404.description: The workspace was not found or this feature is unavailable.

get.description:
Lists current active workspace members in ascending user ID order. Removed
and inactive members, along with service accounts, are excluded. Each result
uses the same `workspace.user` resource and built-in workspace roles as
Get Workspace User.

Pass `email` to resolve an exact email address to a user ID without paging
through the workspace. The response keeps the same list envelope with
zero or one member and `has_more: false`. An unknown email or a user who
is not an active member of this workspace returns an empty list, not a 404.

This list reads from an indexed store and is eventually consistent; it does
not guarantee immediate read-your-write after membership or profile changes.
A newly added member may be absent until the index updates. Without `email`,
a removed or inactive member may briefly remain visible as well.

Use this endpoint when managing current workspace members. The separate
Compliance Users LIST endpoint retains its historical export behavior and
legacy response shape.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: User ID after which to fetch the next page of active members. Cannot be combined with email.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum active members to return. The default is 20 and the maximum is 1000. With email, this limit is still validated, but at most one member is returned.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description:
Exact email address to look up in this workspace, normalized by trimming
surrounding whitespace and lowercasing. Partial and prefix matches are
not supported. Cannot be combined with `after`, including an empty cursor.
URL-encode the address when constructing the query string; for example,
`?email=alex%2Bqa%40example.com` looks up `alex+qa@example.com`.

400.description:
The email, pagination cursor, or limit is invalid. An empty or malformed
email returns `invalid_email`; combining email with `after` returns
`invalid_cursor`.

401.description: Missing or invalid Admin API key.

403.description: Admin API key lacks the required Users scope or workspace access.

404.description: The workspace or cursor member was not found, or this feature is unavailable.

429.description: Too many requests. The endpoint quota, an operation protection, or a downstream limit was exceeded. Follow Retry-After when provided.

Updates an accepted member's built-in workspace role, product seat, or both.
Only workspace owners may update members. SCIM-managed members may receive
role or seat updates when the same change is allowed in Workspace Settings.
The API rejects empty bodies, null values, unknown fields, unsupported
combinations, and changes that would remove the last owner.

delete.description:
Removes accepted workspace membership without deleting the global user or
workspace data. With a Users write Admin API key, workspace owners may remove
members, admins, and owners; workspace admins may remove only lower-role
members. A caller may remove their own membership through the self-leave flow,
except when they are the last owner. The last owner cannot be removed.
SCIM-managed members must be removed through the identity provider.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The auth user ID of the accepted workspace member.

401.description: Missing or invalid Admin API key.

403.description: Admin API key lacks the required Users scope or workspace access, or the actor cannot remove the target member.

404.description: The workspace or member was not found, or this feature is unavailable.

422.description: The deletion would remove the last workspace owner.

get.description:
Lists users assigned to a workspace group.

Results are ordered by membership creation time. Use the returned `cursor` value to fetch
the next page with the same `order`.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The ID of the workspace group.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of users to list. The default is 20 and the maximum is 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous response.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Membership creation-time sort order. Cursors are opaque and stable for this ordering.

400.description: Invalid cursor, limit, or request input.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin API key.

403.description: Admin API key does not have the required group management scope or is not authorized for the workspace.

404.description: The workspace or group was not found.

429.description: Too many requests. The endpoint quota, an operation protection, or a downstream limit was exceeded. Follow Retry-After when provided.

post.description:
Adds a workspace user to a manually managed workspace group.
For up to 100 users, use `POST /manage/workspaces/{workspace_id}/groups/{group_id}/users/bulk`.

This endpoint changes ChatGPT-managed group membership only. If the group is
SCIM-managed, update membership in your identity provider instead; the request
returns `409` with code `scim_managed_resource`.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The ID of the workspace group.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin API key.

403.description: Admin API key does not have the required group management scope or is not authorized for the workspace.

404.description: The workspace, user, or group was not found.

409.description: The membership change conflicts with the current directory state, such as a SCIM-managed group or restricted safe mode policy conflict.

429.description: Too many requests. The endpoint quota, an operation protection, or a downstream limit was exceeded. Follow Retry-After when provided.

delete.description:
Synchronously processes 1–100 distinct users of one manually managed group. The admin
API key must have `chatgpt.enterprise.directory.write` and access to the workspace's
organization. SCIM-managed groups must be changed through SCIM; their per-user results
are 409 `scim_managed_resource`. Existing authorization, eligibility, restricted-safe-mode,
manager-revocation ordering, and required access-control side effects are preserved.

Empty, duplicate, malformed and over-100 batches return 400 before user work. Independent
users run with at most five concurrent operations per request. At most two bulk group
requests are admitted simultaneously per serving process; additional requests return
HTTP 429 with Retry-After before writes. Each HTTP batch consumes one shared
workspace API quota unit.

The batch is not atomic. HTTP 200 returns an array in input order, including every user,
even if every operation fails. A failed or missing user does not discard peer results.
The handler stops admitting users after at most 25 seconds, or one second before its
configured server HTTP deadline, whichever is earlier. Started operations are canceled
and joined; unstarted users return `not_attempted`. Cancellation cleanup can consume
the reserve. A shorter upstream/client timeout can still prevent the whole response.

A started write whose response or side effect failed is `unknown`, not proof of no change.
Never automatically retry an unknown write or a batch with a lost whole response.
Reconcile membership, group-manager assignment and required access-control invalidations
before issuing new intent; checking only the membership edge is insufficient. `failed`
before a write and `not_attempted` may be retried when `retryable` is true, respecting
Retry-After. Successful membership does not guarantee search-index freshness. These
results are not an atomic snapshot and concurrent administrators can make later changes.

Split a 1,000-user operation into ten requests of at most 100 distinct IDs. Keep a durable
ledger keyed by submitted ID, begin with one request in flight, and preserve every result.
Do not replay complete batches to recover individual failures. The 100-user limit is a
request-size limit, not a production latency or throughput guarantee.

Example: `DELETE /v1/manage/workspaces/{workspace_id}/groups/{group_id}/users`
with JSON `{"user_ids":["user-AAA","user-BBB"]}`.

200.description: Complete ordered per-user results; partial and all-failure batches also return HTTP 200.

value.message: Reconcile membership and required access-control side effects before new write intent.

400.description: Missing, empty, duplicate, malformed or oversized user_ids; no user work started.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin API key; no user work started.

403.description: Missing directory-write scope or workspace/organization access; no user work started.

404.description: Workspace not found; no user work started.

429.description: Existing request quota or concurrent bulk admission exceeded; no user work started.
